newsitem.title: USA: Hayes to ship K56Flex line of modems on March 24.
newsitem.headline: Hayes to ship K56Flex line of modems on March 24.

text.p: Hayes Microcomputer Products Inc said Tuesday it will begin shipping its K56Flex line of client modems in the United States the week of March 24.

The company said its 56-kilo-bits-per-second (kbps) ACCURA, Practical Peripherals and PCMCIA modems ought to reach store shelves "several days" after arriving at wholesale distributors and direct retail and mail order accounts.
The cost of 10 K56Flex products will range between $149 and $219 each, it said
The company said it will ship European, Asia and Pacific versions of most of its K56Flex products within four weeks following the domestic launch.
K56Flex is the technology that gives the modems connection speed of up to 56-kbps.
Based in Norcross, Georgia, the company ranks as the second largest consumer modem maker after U.S. Robotics Corp.
On March 14, Rockwell Semiconductor Systems said it was delaying shipment of some its newly introduced K56Flex modem chipsets by up to two weeks in order to make some improvements to the products.
The modem chipsets are used in personal computer or stand-alone end-user modems.
